clipforge_narration_sync.root_cause_notes:
1. Visual-Temporal Desync via Speed/Stretch Mismatch: AI authors select wide footage boundaries (e.g. 26s in cut 0 of hxh6-p9: 1204-1230s) containing multiple actions, while writing a paragraph of voiceover (11.088s TTS). Reconcile scales the entire cut by stretch=0.426. Visual action ('Gon throws his arms up') occurs at source 1205.8s (appears at 0.77s on screen), but the spoken sentence describing it starts at audio second 7.20s, resulting in a measured lag of +6.43s. The picture had already moved past the moment 6.4s prior.
2. Free-floating Narration without Visual Anchors: production.json schema had no visual anchor timestamp field, allowing AI models to guess timing and describe events anywhere within or outside the cut range without temporal binding.
3. Edited Timeline vs Source Timeline Disconnect: The AI author was not instructed on how source timestamps translate through retiming to the edited timeline, leading to cumulative perceptual lag.
4. Stage A Prompt lacked structured screenshot-to-timestamp anchoring tables and worked contrastive examples of anchored vs drifted cuts.
done: B3: Pulled real production.json and rendered output from job hxh6-p9 (workflow run 39163606595), measured actual visual-to-narration offset (+6.43s lag in cut 0)
B3: Determined root causes: wide cut boundaries retimed with stretch, lack of visual_anchor_seconds binding in schema, and free-floating voiceover without timeline derivation
B4: Schema anchoring: added visual_anchor_seconds (and aliases anchor_seconds/visual_anchor) to schemas/production_plan.schema.json, pipeline/plan/schema.py, and site/js/plan.js with range checks

B4: Measured TTS durations & pre-render timeline derivation: reconcile_cuts in render.py aligns visual anchors within lead-in window [0, 0.3s] and expands footage window deterministically when vo exceeds footage
B4: Pre-render validation step: validate_narration_anchors in render.py and validator.py fails fast if narration offset exceeds 0.3s tolerance with actionable error diagnostics
B4: Fix Stage A prompt generator: updated pipeline/plan/prompt.py with visual anchoring guidelines, worked contrastive examples, screenshot timestamp lookup rules, and updated schema
B4: Backward compatibility: existing plans lacking visual_anchor_seconds default anchor to start_seconds with a logged notice rather than failing

B4: Automated regression check: pipeline/tests/test_narration_sync.py added (6 test cases covering anchor sync, window expansion, legacy back-compat, intentional mis-timing detection, and no cumulative drift across multi-cut sequences)
B5: Verification: measured offset reduced from +6.43s to <=0.14s; end-to-end ffmpeg render confirmed green with zero cumulative drift
